title: First Unique Number Stream
description:
You have a stream of integers, and you want to find the **first unique** integer (an integer that has appeared **exactly once** so far, choosing the earliest inserted one) at any time.

Implement the `FirstUnique` class:
- `FirstUnique(int[] nums)` initializes the object with the initial stream elements `nums` in order.
- `int showFirstUnique()` returns the value of the **first unique** integer currently in the stream, or `-1` if no unique integer exists.
- `void add(int value)` appends `value` to the stream.

Both `showFirstUnique` and `add` must run in `O(1)` average time.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to showFirstUnique and add.
hints: Maintain a doubly linked list holding only the currently unique values in insertion order, with sentinel `head` and `tail` nodes.

Keep a hash map from `value` to its list node (or a sentinel `null` once the value has appeared at least twice); on a second occurrence, unlink the node in O(1) so `head.next` is always the first unique value.

examples.explanation: Initial stream [2, 3, 5] has first unique 2; adding 5 duplicates 5 (first unique still 2); adding 2 duplicates 2 (first unique becomes 3); adding 3 duplicates 3 (no unique left -> -1).
Initial stream [7, 7, 7, 7] has no unique values (-1); adding 7 keeps -1; adding 3 makes 3 the first unique.
Starting empty returns -1; adding 10 then 20 makes 10 first unique; adding 10 again promotes 20.
